photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: This is a studio portrait of a named Pawnee chief in full traditional dress—fringed shirt, shell necklace and choker, ear ornaments, fur turban with eagle feathers, and holding a tomahawk—directly documenting Pawnee dress and material culture.

photo.name: photographic print; album
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); album
photo.reason: Studio portrait of Pi-ta-ne-sha-a-du, Principal Chief of the Pawnee, in full regalia (fur/feather headdress, bear claw necklace, warrior shirt, embroidered leggings, moccasins, pipe) — a documentary photograph of Pawnee dress and leadership, directly matching the claimed ethnicity.

photo.name: photographic print; album

photo.reason: This is a studio photograph of a named Pawnee chief in traditional dress (decorated leggings, moccasins, ear ornaments, feather hair ornament) holding a dead eagle, documenting Pawnee attire and material culture.

photo.title: carte-de-visite (black and white)
photo.reason: A studio carte-de-visite portrait of a Pawnee man wearing a feather, ear-ring and neck ornament, draped in a blanket and holding a tomahawk pipe — a documentary photo of dress and adornment matching the claimed people.

photo.name: photographic print; album

photo.reason: Studio portrait of four Pawnee chiefs in traditional dress—decorated leggings, moccasins, peace medals, ear ornaments, a bear claw necklace and turban—holding tomahawks and a rifle, a documentary photograph of Pawnee dress and regalia.

photo.name: carte-de-visite

photo.reason: This is a studio carte-de-visite portrait of a Pawnee man wearing a headband, chains, pendants, and a buffalo robe wrapped around his waist — documentary photographic evidence of Pawnee dress and adornment.

photo.name: photographic print; album

photo.reason: This is a studio portrait photograph of a Pawnee man wearing traditional dress elements—cloth shirt, beaded/shell necklaces, shell ear ornaments, and a roach/eagle feather hairstyle—consistent with 19th-century documentary photography of Plains peoples.

photo.name: photographic print; carte-de-visite

photo.reason: This is a 19th-century studio carte-de-visite portrait of a Native American man wearing a cloth headscarf, ear ornaments, and a blanket, consistent with the claimed Pawnee identity though the museum itself notes uncertainty ("Omaha(?)"); documentary photographs of dress and daily life are valid evidence for the culture.

photo.reason: This is a 19th-century studio portrait of a Pawnee man and woman in traditional dress (fur robe, blanket, shell ear ornaments, braided hair), documenting their attire — a documentary photo of dress fits the claimed ethnicity.

household.name: baby-carrier
household.title: baby-carrier
household.reason: This is a wooden cradleboard/baby-carrier with a carved and painted sunburst design at the top, a well-documented Pawnee craft item used for carrying infants.

household.name: tie; tether
household.title: tie; tether (?)
household.reason: The image shows a leather rein/tether with fringed straps, red flannel wrapping, quillwork, brass bells, and a perforated leather disc with a star motif—consistent with Pawnee horse gear ornamentation. This is a made object attributed to the Pawnee, matching the claimed ethnicity.

arms.name: shield
arms.title: shield
arms.reason: A painted rawhide war shield with a red disc, crescent/claw motifs, and feather attachment—consistent with Plains warfare regalia and museum-attributed to Pawnee manufacture.

arms.name: arrow
arms.title: arrow
arms.reason: The image shows a set of wooden arrows with metal points, feather fletching, and sinew binding, matching the museum's attribution to Pawnee makers; arrows are a plausible traditional Plains weapon type.
